newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish first reinsurer aims to cut premium outflow.
newsitem.headline: Polish first reinsurer aims to cut premium outflow.

text.p: Poland's first reinsurance firm Polskie Towarzystwo Reasekuracyjne SA (PTR) should cut the flow of premiums abroad once its capital is high enough to make it a major market player, a deputy finance minister said.

"We hope that the development of PTR would reduce the outflow of insurance premiums flowing abroad as reinsurance ... but it needs to boost capital to $50 million, only such capital would allow PTR to develop its activities," Jan Bogutyn said.
Now the PTR, a non-life reinsurer in operation since last month, has a 65.2 million zloty ($23.3 million) share capital. @
So far a lack of adequate capital forced most Polish insurers to spend about 40 percent of collected premiums on reinsurance abroad.
Last year Polish insurers collected a total of 5.6 billion zlotys in gross premiums.
PTR's president told Reuters at the company's official launch, the firm, would not eliminate foreign firms but would offer Polish insurers an alternative to foreign reinsurance.
"If we are able to reduce the outflow of premiums by 20 percent in the next three years, it will be our success," Krzysztof Jarmuszczak said.

Main PTR shareholders are state-owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU), its subsidary PZU Life, state-owned bank Bank Handlowy SA, Polish copper concern KGHM and the state treasury -- each holding 19.18 percent stakes in the firm.
Industrial and trading conglomerate Elektrim and TUiR Warta insurer have 1.92-percent stakes each. Polisa SA and PTU Energo-Asekuracja insurers hold the remaining shares.
Jarmuszczak said PTR wanted to issue new shares to domestic and foreign passive investors in the first quarter of 1997 to boost its capital to at least 100 million zlotys. @
He also said the PTR wanted to expand abroad, mainly to Poland's eastern neighbours.

"We want to, and we have to expand as we need to share the risk, and we think of countries at the similar stage of insurance sector development such the Baltic states and perhaps also such as Greece or Portugal," he said.
Jarmuszczak said PTR has already signed six reinsurance agreements and was negotiating further deals.
A deputy president of PZU, Poland's biggest insurer, also present, said PZU would use PTR's services but would still have to reinsure a large portion of its portfolio abroad.

"The capacity of PTR is limited because its capital...is too small for a giant such as PZU, but we will certainly watch its growth and increase the premium insured in the firm," Elzbieta Turkowska-Tyrluk said.

Bogutyn said the ministry was considering setting up a reinsurer for life companies but said it was too early to give details and the final decision's would depend on the pace of this segment's development.
